COVID: Field Hospital Beds

By: Mosibudi Ratlebjane | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
ICU Units Assembled in less than 45 min

Unique Selling Point:
ICU unites and beds that are able to be assembled like puzzle like pieces in under 45minutes.Designed to help the scourge of the Covid-19 pandemic to assist the overburdened need for hospitals beds, and ICU units in South Africa.

Summary:
Inter Market Graphics, is the company that has established these beds made out of boards. Together with Zanita, the company that manufactures the boards, have come up with this novel idea to use biodegradable boards to be used as ICU units, that can be assembled in 45 minutes.

Set as a solution for South Africans, tested positive for, Covid-19 to be have a bed that could be assembled and placed in hospitals, Town halls and churches, around the country. This is as a measure to relief the shortages of beds, as witnessed in medical facilities in countries worst hit by Covid-19.



Further information:
The Boards are made by a compressed fibre closed cell board, which makes it much stronger than just a normal cardboard box. This means that the board is strong enough to withstand, getting wet, thus can be wiped down with sanitizer, and reused for another patient.

A proudly South African product, these flat packed boards, have already being exported to countries like Australia, and the US in efforts to use them as biodegradable coffins and beds.

Inter Market Graphics are using this idea, as a solution for government, and have been using, local printing and signage companies to cut these boards. This has brought some relief to the some printing companies like Michael Rasmussen owner of Excel Print. Who have been out of business, due to the lockdown. Should these bed be rolled out nationally, printing companies like Excel Print, can come back to business as. Most printing companies have the correct machinery to cut the boards and ready to be assembled like puzzle pieces.

Press Release:


Field Hospital Beds
With over 5000 recorded infections – of which almost 4000 were confirmed over a four-week period – South Africa is gearing up for an increase in COVID-19 patients as the country begins to ease its lockdown regulations. In preparation, hotels and convention centres are being converted into makeshift healthcare centres and field hospitals are being created in every province. Now some local innovators have come up with an ingenious design that makes affordable, quick-to-assemble and easily sanitised beds available to government.
Producer: Mosibudi Ratlebjane | Presenter: Claire Mawisa


Script:


INSERT SCRIPT:
VISUALS:
VOICE:


VOICE: The National Department of Health projects that the peak of South Africa’s Covid-19 Infections could emerge around August and September, bringing about the need for temporary field hospitals, with Intensive Care Unit units and beds.
Spotting what could become a gap in the market, a signage and graphics company devised what it calls a cost-effective, biodegradable bed and ICU partition that takes all of 45 minutes to set up, says Alister McCreadie.


Clip Number: 00021 Alister McCreadie [0:01:43.710] Well we believe that the hospitals won't be able to facilitate the number of beds that are going to be needed. And the solution would be that we would need a rapid response to this in terms of the manufacturing of hospital beds and the partitioning. Well so with a rapid response in terms of installation.

Printing Machines: Cutting the Boards:


Clip NUmber: AS6I8044_1
Panning close up of how the board looks on the inside:

Clip Number: AS6I8089_1: Boards being taken out like puzzle pieces.
VOICE: The light, closed-cell boards are manufactured from compressed fibre – it’s reusable, durable and strong enough to carry a body, mattress and bedding totalling over 200 kilograms.


Clip Number: 00021 Alister McCreadie [00:02:16.320] Well the Zinita Board is a need to bring on board a locally manufactured board that we produce here. The sheets are all to be able to cut this board into various shapes and sizes to put partitioning and the beds together.
VOICE: Local printing and signage companies like Excel Print, shut down for the lockdown, can scale up the manufacture at short notice – and the group is engaging private and government partners in the hopes of rolling out their beds nationwide.

Clip Number: AS6I8033_1_AUDIO.M4A
Mike Rasmussen (02:00:11:030) We're very grateful to them for this opportunity because not only does it enable us to earn some money during the lockdown period to pay our staff and take care of our people but it's also getting involved in a project that is going to make a huge difference in our country and save lives.
VOICE: From town halls to tents, the beds and room dividers come flat-packed – easy to sanitize between patients and just as easy to relocate, to where the need is greatest.


Alister McCreadie 00:03:11:190: Well firstly we've come up with two unit types. The first unit top we've constructed where you have two beds. You have a real wall and a center partitioning one of these units with the beds could be put together with three people would only take 45 minutes. So a set of 10 would then give you 20 beds 10 on one side and 10 on the other side.
